canonical_name: Bezos Scholars Program
notes: Open only to U.S. Citizens, Permanent Residents, and DACA students, plus a small separate 5-scholar Africa track. Türkiye is not an eligible country under either track.

canonical_name: Diller Teen Fellows
notes: For Jewish teens (10th-11th grade) in 32 specific partner communities across 7 countries/regions (US, Canada, UK, Australia, Argentina, South Africa, Israel). Türkiye is not among the listed Diller Global Network communities.

canonical_name: World Youth Forum (Egypt)
notes: Open to ages 18-40; excludes the great majority of high-school-aged students. Fully funded and passport-open internationally, but age floor makes it a poor fit for this lane's target user.

canonical_name: Legacy International / U.S. State Dept Youth Leadership Program — Turkey track
notes: A Turkish-and-U.S. high-school agricultural leadership exchange existed 2019-2020 but is no longer listed among Legacy International's currently active State Department-funded youth programs (current list: Fiji/Tonga/Tuvalu, Finland/Sweden/UK, Africa 2025). No current Turkey pathway found.

canonical_name: YouthActionNet Laureate Global Fellowship (International Youth Foundation)
notes: Program operated 2001-2019 and is explicitly marked as ended by its own host page; also skewed ages 18-29 even when active.

canonical_name: Plan International UK Youth Advisory Panel
notes: Eligibility explicitly requires being 'based in the UK.' Ages 14-19 would otherwise fit well, but UK residency is a hard requirement.

canonical_name: British Council Active Citizens programme (Turkey)
notes: British Council's own materials describe Active Citizens as having run 'from 2009 to 2021' — discontinued. No current British Council Turkey youth leadership program (beyond postgraduate scholarships, which are out of this lane's scope) was found to replace it.

canonical_name: Genç TEMA (TEMA Foundation youth volunteer organization)
notes: Organizer's own page explicitly defines Genç TEMA as 'Üniversitede Gönüllülük' — 'Üniversite öğrencilerinden oluşan gönüllü örgütlenmemizdir' (a volunteer organization made up of university students). No high-school pathway found. (Separately, the school-delivered 'Lise TEMA Eğitim Programı' is a teacher-led curriculum add-on, not an individually-joinable student opportunity, so it was not recorded either.)

canonical_name: National Geographic Young Explorers Grant
notes: Ages 18-25 only; not accessible to typical high school students.

canonical_name: Resolution Project Social Venture Challenge / Resolution Fellowship
notes: 'High school and graduate students may participate as Venture Team members, but are not eligible to receive Resolution Fellowships' — founder/Fellow status (the actual award) is restricted to enrolled undergraduates. A high schooler could only be a secondary team member, not the lead awardee, so this is a poor primary opportunity for our target user.

canonical_name: European Forum Alpbach Scholarship / Junior Fellowship
notes: Standard eligibility is ages 18-30 (18-35 for Global South citizens); in practice targets young adults, not high schoolers. Technically some just-turned-18 students could qualify, but this is not a good fit for the target age band as a rule.

canonical_name: WWF-Türkiye general volunteer programme (Topluluk/Uzman/Proje/Ofis Gönüllüleri)
notes: Organizer's own volunteer page requires being 'over 18 years old.' Kept separate from — and should not be confused with — the youth-specific 'Doğa Öncüleri' programme (accepted in batch2), which is explicitly for grades 5-7 and lise students.

canonical_name: Best Buddies International (Turkey chapter)
notes: Real, well-documented US-founded high-school leadership/inclusion chapter model globally, but no evidence of an active Turkey chapter was found in available sources.

canonical_name: Kluz Prize for PeaceTech
notes: Targets established technology projects/organizations/startups with a track record, not individual high school students; not a fit for this lane.

canonical_name: Encode Justice
notes: The official encodejustice.org domain now 301-redirects to encodeai.org, whose homepage in 2026 shows no visible youth/student chapter program (only a funder acknowledgment mentioning a 'Responsible Technology Youth Power Fund'). Could not confirm whether Encode Justice still operates as a distinct, joinable youth chapter network as of this research date. Needs direct re-verification, not a source we could confidently mark eligible.

canonical_name: Global Youth Biodiversity Network (GYBN) — Turkey access
notes: Real, UN-CBD-recognized global youth network with regional chapters (e.g. GYBN Europe+), but our fetch tool was blocked (403) on gybn.org and gybn.org/get-involved/, and no source found explicitly confirmed a Turkey member organization or chapter. Do not add without direct confirmation.

canonical_name: Aile ve Gençlik Bankası / Aile ve Gençlik Fonu
notes: IMPORTANT CORRECTION: despite the name suggesting a youth social-innovation micro-grant scheme, this is in fact an interest-free MARRIAGE LOAN fund for newlywed couples aged 18-29. Entirely unrelated to youth leadership/social impact; flagging explicitly so a future researcher does not waste time re-investigating this name.

canonical_name: AKUT Gençlik (AKUT Arama Kurtarma Derneği youth pathway)
notes: AKUT's standard volunteer/operational training pathway appears university-student/adult oriented (search-and-rescue field work implies 18+ for safety/legal reasons); no distinct, standardized high-school-age program was found.

canonical_name: Common Purpose youth leadership programmes
notes: Common Purpose runs various leadership programmes (e.g. regional 'Young Leaders' tracks), but no clearly-documented, currently-open programme specifically for ages 15-18 with international (Turkey-inclusive) eligibility could be located.

canonical_name: Toplum Gönüllüleri Vakfı (TOG)
notes: TOG's local-group volunteering structure is organized around ~124 university locations for enrolled university students; a TOG scholarship track exists but is also for university students. No standard high-school pathway found.

canonical_name: Türkiye Gençlik Konseyi (TGK)
notes: Search results returned an ambiguous mix of a 'Türkiye Gençlik Konseyi' site and a Wikipedia entry for 'Youth Union of Turkey,' raising uncertainty about the organization's exact nature and whether it is politically affiliated. Not enough independent verification of a neutral, individually-joinable, output-based opportunity to responsibly recommend — deliberately excluded rather than risk recommending a politically-affiliated group without disclosure.

canonical_name: Rotary RYLA (Rotary Youth Leadership Awards) — Türkiye districts
notes: RYLA genuinely runs in Türkiye (Rotary districts 2420/2430/2440), but is organized per-district/per-club with nomination through a local Rotary club rather than a single central application; the specific district page we fetched described Rotary Youth Exchange (RYE, ages 15-25) rather than a standalone RYLA eligibility page. Could not locate one authoritative, citable official eligibility page to meet the evidence bar — worth a future researcher's more targeted, district-by-district follow-up.

canonical_name: Sivil Düşün AB Programı — individual/Activist track
notes: This EU-funded program does support 'individuals' as well as organizations in principle (Activist Program / Small Grants), but no source confirmed a minor (under-18) could independently hold and administer an EU grant; realistically appears to function as an 18+ pathway. Deprioritized pending clearer confirmation.

canonical_name: Gençlik Projeleri Destekleme Programı (T.C. Gençlik ve Spor Bakanlığı)
notes: Individuals aged 15-29 can in principle be involved (with parental consent under 18), but the applicant unit is an organization type (civil society organization, university, high school, youth group, public institution) rather than a lone individual student, and the page we fetched stated no project call was currently open. Deprioritized: real but not a clean self-application opportunity for a single student, and not currently active.

canonical_name: Y-PEER Türkiye (Sağlıkta Genç Yaklaşımlar Derneği) — general volunteer peer-educator track
notes: Real, UNFPA/UNICEF-linked national organization (est. 2015) with periodic volunteer recruitment, but we could not confirm from official sources that general peer-educator volunteering is open to high-school-age (15-18) youth specifically — one specific programme track we found targeted women aged 18-25. Deprioritized pending age confirmation.

canonical_name: Bilim Kahramanları Derneği (Science Heroes Association) volunteering
notes: Standard volunteering (referee/jury/observer roles at FIRST LEGO League-style tournaments) requires being 18+ per the organizer; under-18 volunteering is only handled ad hoc ('should contact the association'). Also, the underlying activity is mostly organizing competitions for younger children rather than a leadership program for the teen volunteer themselves.

canonical_name: Yeşilay Kamp Lideri Yetiştirme Programı (Camp Leader Training)
notes: This specific leadership track requires already being an active Yeşilay volunteer for at least 1 year with prior peer-educator/trainer experience — a second-tier program, not a usable entry point for a student who is not already a longstanding Yeşilay volunteer. General Yeşilay volunteering exists but its base age eligibility was not confirmed.
